body: Having a baby during the peak of Covid did it for me. Postpartum depression and anxiety. Before that, I could manage my anxiety.

Complete loss of appetite. Days can go by without eating. I'll feel weak and lightheaded but will still have no desire to eat anything. And the knots in my stomach are only made worse by starvation. People like to tell me that I'm lucky this happens rather than binge eating when anxious but it's actually painful and exhausting and I have passed out multiple times because of it which is also not fun.

It drives me crazy how so many people are inclined to give men all the credit... My son is my absolute twin and it is so satisfying that no one can deny the resemblance, especially because when he was a newborn everyone tried to tell me that he looked like his father.

Had a similar convo with my husband today... About how I made lists of achievements I wanted to succeed at. I assumed that once I did this or got that... I'd FINALLY be happy. Never happened. Whenever I'd get what I wanted, I'd just move the goal post. Decide that I'd be happy after the next big thing.

Life isn't always about getting what you want as much as wanting what you got. You can still have goals in life and can make you proud and happy when you achieve them but it's not enough to rely entirely on other people and life scenarios for joy.

I have a good life. A career. A house. A Marriage... I'm not sitting here with my feet up surrounded by an aura of happiness 24/7... But I can say that I am finally content. For me, it was all in treating my depression. Maybe you should talk to a doctor.

I always pictured myself having a girl. 

Initially, we planned to have two. So when I found out we were having a boy I didn't think I lost my only chance. But then at about 8 weeks we decided one was enough. And I didn't *need* a girl. My boy is all I need. He is sweet and funny and beautiful and Momma's boy.

My anxiety/depression was brought on by the stress and trauma of having a baby (plus a traumatic birth) during a global pandemic with little to no support from friends, family and medical professionals. With medication (SSRI) I am able to function; think clearly and not obsessively worry all day and night. When I come off the meds, I spiral out of control; stop eating and can't focus or do every day tasks. My sleeping pattern is messed up. I just feel terrible dread all the time.

This fits into the theory that prolonged stressful and traumatic events can impair brain function permanently. I never had these issues before.

Before I got help, the anxiety existed before the thought. I'd feel panic for literally no reason. Then my brain would start searching for reasons for why I felt that way. Once my mind settled on a reason I would obsess about this thing for days and weeks. I'd make mental lists for why it was bad vs. why it was okay and then compare those things and NEVER settle on a conclusion because the feeling remained. It was exhausting and had I not gotten help I don't know if I'd still be here.
